details:
Build 993 | Valve Index | Windows 10 | Steam Version of VRC

If you already have an instance of VRChat running, and use the website to generate a protocol link to a world, running it will cause your controls in-game to break and Steam to see that instance of VRChat as an non-Steam program.
When recording my repro steps for it, it did not occur to me the first time I tried to do it, but it did the subsequent time. When in this state, selecting "VRChat" in the Steam dashboard will cause that instance to close and a new instance to open (as Steam does not see VRChat as being open).
This breaks finger tracking on Index controllers, making it unable to curl your fingers. It also causes any input to be interpreted as a gesture toggle in addition to the default action. You can still open your menu, move, and turn. It does not make the game unplayable, but it certainly is not worth playing in that state. A simple restart fixes this.
I was not able to find any glaring errors in the log files, apart from the faulty instance sporting a "Failed to start OSC Server..". This appears to be a sound related thing and the server is started right after this error, so i don't believe it is important.

Repro Steps:
1. Start an instance of VRChat (Can be from Steam or from a protocol link).
2. Once loaded in, ensure controls work. Try to open up another protocol link to a world.
3. You will see VRC close and another instance start. Once loaded in, observe controls. You should see that they do not work as intended. May need to do another instance if it does not reproduce on the first try.
4. Look at the Steam Dashboard to see that "VRChat" is running but seemingly as an external program.
5. Restart VRChat to fix.
Video of Repro Steps:
https://youtu.be/8TW9xCUjPys

Output Logs:
First Instance (Working): https://tinyurl.com/VRCControlBugLog1
Second Instance (Broken): https://tinyurl.com/VRCControlBugLog2

title: [933] Controls Break When Starting Instance From Website When Instance Is Already Running
